changes: Removed crypto.randomUUID from the extension, including map visits, teleport epochs, region and waypoint creation, encounter chat IDs and related media slots. Local IDs work on LAN HTTP; existing saved identifiers stay valid.
Map character assignments use an Add character to location button and a searchable wardrobe-style portrait grid. Current residents appear above the grid; selected portraits are blue.

Moving a character from another location requires an explicit source/destination confirmation. Cancel preserves the assignment. Confirm moves the character uniquely without changing their original default home.
Recorded the original default locations for 57 previously imported residents. Default locations and current placements are separate.

New group arrivals away from the default home request a fresh greeting through the native main API, with the exact full character card, chat context, player name and current location. Written card greetings remain unchanged.

Default-home arrivals use the main written location greeting. Generated greetings are saved as ordinary character messages. Pending arrivals survive solo-to-group copying and can be retried after API failure, without duplicate greetings or wrong-location fallbacks.
Retained atomic Teleport companion questions, protected party members, deferred group updates, regional classification and historical scene handling.

limits: Model generation and native message integration were tested with mocked APIs and disposable preview chats. No live model call was made.
Phone viewport checks do not reproduce a physical iPhone Safari keyboard, pinch zoom or compositor behavior.
Shared location assignments and original default homes are settings; companion travel placements and pending greetings belong to each chat.
Dynamic arrivals require a connected main API. Failed requests stay queued for Retry location guests rather than using a home greeting in the wrong place.
Existing map limitations remain: distances are straight-line estimates, classification stays region locked, and high-resolution remote tiles require network access.
